title: ID0438604-DC/Si-D/AT- [RVP / T6 170004787] Charger issue
description:
Reported behavior/issue: After remotely restarting the charger, I noticed that based on the
sound, the charger tried to switch on the QA1, but it seems there
were problems.
The sound is clearly audible in the video, and directly after the QA1
(assumption) rattled for an extended period, smoke came from the
charger.
Please analyze the problem in more detail.
When opening the door, I noticed that the surge arrester (FA12) of
the DC supply had triggered.
Furthermore, before the restart, I noticed that the FC16 was
blinking red rapidly, and re-securing it by briefly pressing was not
possible.
Solution: Replace FA12

additional_info.subject: ID0438604-DC/Si-D/AT- [RVP / T6 170004787] Charger issue CRM:02832000229
additional_info.body:
Hi Johannes,
As you have shown, the FA12 is burned and needs to be replaced.
The investigation must start from the replacement. If you replace the FA12 and the charger is working perfectly again, solution given.
But we still need to understand what kind of signal is coming from the External usage, what is used here in the FA12 input? External E-stop?
I send in attachment the datasheet of the FA12, please check with the customer what kind of signal they are using.
Let me know your feedback.
Best regards,
Francisco

additional_info.subject: AW: ID0438604-DC/Si-D/AT- [RVP / T6 170004787] Charger issue CRM:02832000229
additional_info.body:
Hi Francisco,
yes, we have to change the FA12.
Electrician install all three SID in serial in our emergency line.
Could you also look at the video?
I suspect the smoke isn't coming from the FA12.
When you listen to the sound, the input contactor couldn't switch through and was chattering.
Therefore, I rather think the QA1 caused the smoke.
Could this have come from the feedback line?
Why did the QA1 chatter so strangely?
Do we need to replace the QA1?
I also noticed that the FC16 was flashing very quickly and could not be reset/secured.
You can check it in my video
😊
Kind regards,
Johannes

additional_info.subject: ID0438604-DC/Si-D/AT- [RVP / T6 170004787] Charger issue CRM:02832000229
additional_info.body:
Hi Johannes,
The problem here is that we need to remove the FA12 out of the equation in order to prove that.
If FA12 is burned and causing a short circuit, obviously FC16 will not come to green. We need to replace FA12 and continue from there.
The best I can say is to bring a spare FC16 to site but Mainbreaker I cannot say 100%.
The problem here is that the mainbreaker could've caused the smoke since we were continuously triggering and untriggering QA26 safety relay responsible for the QA1 operation. That's most likely why you hear the noise from the contactors opening and closing.
Let me know your feedback.
Best regards,
Francisco

additional_info.subject: AW: ID0438604-DC/Si-D/AT- [RVP / T6 170004787] Charger issue CRM:02832000229
additional_info.body:
So if we change FA12 it should be fine.
If FC16 is still blinking we should also change.
Is it safe to start up the charger after we have replaced the FA12?
I want to avoid another smoking incident and thus triggering of the QA1, since we are located at a gas station and a fire here could have serious consequences.
Best regards,
Johannes
